body:
Hi @binarykitchen,

I think this is more likely a Chrome bug, as the download button is a UI feature that is not part of the spec. (Just like the play button, in fact.) All the spec says about video UI is in vague phrases such as

> If the attribute is present, or if scripting is disabled for the media element, then the user agent should expose a user interface to the user. This user interface should include features to begin playback, pause playback, seek to an arbitrary position in the content (if the content supports arbitrary seeking), change the volume, change the display of closed captions or embedded sign-language tracks, select different audio tracks or turn on audio descriptions, and show the media content in manners more suitable to the user (e.g. fullscreen video or in an independent resizable window). Other controls may also be made available.

which are intentionally left vague so as to allow user agents to innovate on user experience. The download button you mention is indeed one such innovation.

As such, I'm hopeful that Chrome should be able to create a better implementation of it that uses the filename from the server. But, it is probably out of scope for the spec to tell them that.

I'll close this, but thanks for thinking of us when you encountered this. And if you think my reasoning was wrong, let me know, and we can continue discussing and potentially reopen the issue.
